question: Article 12(1) of the recast EU Energy Efficiency Directive1 requires that data centres above a certain size make publicly available information related to a few different factors, including energy consumption, waste heat utilisation and water usage. Article 12(3) of the same directive mandates the Commission to establish a European database to collect the information disclosed by data centres.

According to this article, this information will then be made available to the public in an aggregated form. The Irish Government has stated2 that it does not intend to have a national database through which data centres will make the required information available to the public.
Instead, the Irish Government envisages that data centres based in Ireland will fulfil the Article 12(1) requirement by reporting directly to the European database. 1.
Will this European database allow the public to access the required reporting information for individual, identifiable data centres, and not only aggregated information?

If not, can Member States be said to be complying with their Article 12(1) obligations, if they only require data centres to submit the relevant information to the European database, with no other means of making this information publicly accessible?

Directive (EU) 2023/1791 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 September 2023 on energy efficiency, OJ L 231, 20.9.2023, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/1791/oj. https://www.oireachtas.ie/en/debates/question/2024-1008/40/?highlight%5B0%5D=data&highlight%5B1%5D=centres&highlight%5B2%5D=data&highlight%5B3 %5D=centres&highlight%5B4%5D=data.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.1.2025) Article 5(5) of the Delegated Regulation 2024/13641 (Delegated Act) states that the European database on data centres cannot be accessed by the public.

In accordance with Article 12(3) of recast Energy Efficiency Directive2 (EED recast), the public will have access only to the aggregated data (via a webpage, currently under development), which are described in detail in Annex IV of the Delegated Act.

Thus, only asking data centre operators to communicate the relevant data and information to the European database, without other means of making this information publicly accessible, would not be adequate for the fulfilment of the Member States’ obligations under Article 12(1) of the EED recast.
1 Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 of 14 March 2024 on the first phase of the establishment of

a common Union rating scheme for data centres: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2024/1364/oj 2 Directive (EU) 2023/1791 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 September 2023 on energy efficiency and amending Regulation (EU) 2023/955 (recast): http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/1791/oj
